# Square-wave corrugated seafloor, 25 Hz: transmission loss from a two-way coupled-mode solution.
# 
# Problem: Evans, R. B. and Gilbert, K. E., "The periodic extension of stepwise coupled modes",
# J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 77, 983-988 (1985). Isovelocity water 1500 m/s, density 1.0, 100 m
# deep, over a homogeneous fluid bottom 1704.5 m/s, density 2.5, 0.5 dB/wavelength. Between
# 5 and 10 km the seafloor is a square wave: 90 m deep on [5.00 + 0.1 k, 5.05 + 0.1 k) km
# and 100 m deep on [5.05 + 0.1 k, 5.10 + 0.1 k) km, k = 0..49 (10 m high, 100 m period);
# 100 m deep elsewhere. Source 18 m, receiver 50 m.
# 
# Solution: COUPLE07 (R. B. Evans, December 2007 version, distributed by OALIB as
# Modes/couple/couple07.zip), its own Test Case 3 input run unchanged: 120 modes,
# cylindrical geometry, 101 regions, the fully two-way solution matching pressure and
# radial particle velocity (IOUT = 0), and the source backed by an absorber at negative
# range (IREFL = 1). The COUPLE documentation notes that the 2.5 density makes the
# multiply scattered field significant. COUPLE closes the bottom with a pressure-release
# boundary at 1500 m below a homogeneous 0.5 dB/wavelength sediment. Rerun with 200 modes
# the table moves by 0.11 dB of mean or less in each of the 0.25-5, 5-10 and 10-18 km
# windows, so it is converged in mode count. Built with gfortran -std=legacy and stubs for the Lahey TIMER/DATE
# intrinsics; runtime ~18 s. Only this generated table is shipped: the COUPLE source
# carries no licence.
# 
# TL is dB re 1 m; the range-zero row COUPLE prints is omitted.
# 
# range_km  TL_50m_dB
